prose: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's largest DRAM maker, announced its fifth-generation technology platform has entered mass production, with vice president Luo Xiaodong claiming its process capability is now on par with the most advanced mass-produced nodes in the industry and that the memory shortage cannot last until 2030.

The platform specs an 11.95nm active area half-pitch and a 45:1 storage capacitor aspect ratio using four-exposure patterning, yielding at least 50% more dies per wafer than the fourth generation on an 8Gb baseline. Two 24Gb LPDDR5X products already run on it - in 496-ball and 245-ball packages for mid-range and high-end handsets - and Reuters reports CXMT is pitching the platform to electronics makers as an additional source of supply, aiming squarely at buyers currently choosing between Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.
highlights: CXMT claims process parity with the industry's most advanced mass-produced DRAM nodes.
Fifth-gen platform in mass production: 11.95nm half-pitch, 45:1 capacitor aspect ratio, four-exposure patterning.
Yields at least 50% more dies per wafer than gen four on an 8Gb baseline.
First products: two 24Gb LPDDR5X chips for mid-range and high-end phones.
Pitched as an alternative supply source to Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.
